a16z's Angela Strange sits down with @Valon's Andrew Wang and Linda Du to unpack what it takes to rebuild the infrastructure underneath a $13 trillion mortgage market that still relies heavily on systems designed before the internet.

Linda and Andrew explain why Valon chose the hardest path: becoming a regulated mortgage servicer, translating decades of federal and state regulation into software, and proving the platform on its own loans before selling it to the industry. That foundation made Valon roughly 3x as efficient as traditional servicing and created the system of record it is now using to bring AI into complex mortgage workflows.

They also discuss what AI makes possible on top of that infrastructure, from agents handling long-tail servicing tasks to voice interfaces and more personalized customer experiences. And they explain why deploying the technology into large regulated enterprises is ultimately as much a change-management challenge as a technical one.

Employment Friday delivered a split report: non-farm payrolls came in well below expectations while household employment rose more than 400,000. But Cathie Wood opened this month's episode somewhere unusual, with a tweet from Bill Ackman.

Ackman's argument is that rising interest costs could feed a vicious inflation cycle. Cathie Wood says she first heard that case in the late 1970s, when inflation was stuck in double digits. She believes this period looks far more like the 1980s, when productivity drove real growth up and an early technology revolution drove inflation down.

The 10-year Treasury yield is now above 5%, after dipping below 1% during COVID. Pulling the chart back to 1790, Cathie Wood says 5% sits near the midpoint of American history, though higher than during large stretches of it. In our view, the anomaly was not today, it was the spike from the 1970s through COVID, which she traces to the closing of the gold window in 1971.

Abstract is winding down.

Starting today, all of @IglooInc's focus will go towards taking Pudgy Penguins, Pudgy NFTs, and $PENGU to the next level.

When we acquired Frame in the summer of 2024, the vision was to build the blockchain for consumer crypto. Pudgy Penguins had shown us what it meant to reach the masses, and we believed we could bring that same approach to building a chain.

Abstract achieved a lot in a short period of time; we built the Portal and AGW, onboarded major global brands, amassed over 300 million transactions, and grew a vibrant onchain ecosystem. 

The journey became stifled by the lack of a DeFi ecosystem, insufficient liquidity, minimal institutional cross-over, and prohibitively high costs that impeded growth in winning areas.

Unknown to most, Igloo, Inc. had been funding Abstract over the last 18 months.

After losing tens of millions of dollars over two years, building consumer products, assembling an all-star team, onboarding some of the biggest brands in the world, and building a community of millions, we still had not found product-market fit.

In combination with the market's reduced appetite for what we had built and not being able to find a scalable path forward, we could no longer justify taking from the Pudgy Penguins business.

Igloo, Inc. has always been a community-first company. Even after losing 8 figures, we could have launched a token or pursued an ICO.

Ultimately we decided against this. A token only works if there is something driving demand to it, and launching a token that we don’t have conviction in would have been a disservice to our community.

The entire team at Abstract has worked tirelessly with a tremendous amount of passion to make the consumer crypto vision come true. I cannot fault a single one of them for this outcome.

To the Abstract community, I want to thank all of you for sticking by our side on this long journey and for continuing to champion us. You supported us through all of the ups and downs, and I wish the result could have been different.

There will be many that will find satisfaction in seeing this shut down, and that is fine. I take a great amount of pride in having the ambition to venture into the chain business, notoriously one of the most difficult to make work, and the only regret I have is not being able to celebrate a win alongside the Abstract community.

As we wind down Abstract, our full focus shifts to making Pudgy Penguins into the global & cultural phenomenon I know it can become. 

Return to Pudgy Penguins.

I’m extremely sad to announce that Abstract is shutting down.

When we were just a three-person team building Frame I never could have imagined the two and half year journey I was about to embark on.

From the tireless nights preparing for launch, to mainnet going live in January 2025, and everything in between, this journey is one I will treasure for the rest of my life. Even though the outcome is not what we wanted, I am incredibly proud of everything we built at Abstract.

The Portal and Abstract Global Wallet made interacting with a blockchain feel seamless. That foundation led to a wave of unique apps, novel onchain experiences, and, most importantly, an incredibly passionate community that gave Abstract an identity and culture of its own.

But the truth is that the industry has changed significantly since the idea was first conceived in the summer of 2024, and Abstract was facing difficulties with our DeFi Ecosystem and liquidity on the chain.

We reached a crossroads of experiencing significant growth, but not having cemented product-market-fit,and that was becoming an issue from a business sustainability perspective.

A very difficult decision needed to be made. Abstract’s growth had stalled and the chain was simply not economically sustainable anymore despite our best efforts.

I am extremely grateful to the Igloo, Inc team who truly gave it their all to explore every angle and make Abstract work.

I want to take this time to thank the incredibly talented team I had the pleasure of working with over the last three years. Every single one of them poured their heart and soul into Abstract and together we created something truly special that pushed forward what onchain discovery and experiences could look like. It is the best team that I have ever worked with. I will always be proud of that.

I want to thank all of our partners and builders that worked with us to make Abstract such a unique, special place. Truly some of the most talented developers launched on Abstract and I know you will all kill it in your next chapter.

Most of all I want to thank the Abstract community for the support over these three years. I know there have been moments of frustration, but your passion and admiration for Abstract are what made it so special and helped create a culture that is incredibly rare in crypto. I truly wish this could have worked out for all of us.

Thank you for supporting the green chain ✳️

David Friedberg: The AI Wars Are Already Here, and America Can’t Hit Pause

“We always assumed in the sci-fi novels that we would be in an era of having robot wars, and I think we failed to recognize that the software came first, and we are actually having the AI wars.

I think we will see a massive rise in defense systems. What I heard in DC this week was some Fortune 50 CEOs are very worried about cyber defense.

That means they're going to start to make this their #1 priority to address at the board level. That means the budgets for cyber defense are going to go through the roof.

Now, let me ask you a question. When you have to do cyber defense in an era of AI, are you going to use old school software, or are you going to use AI?

You're going to use AI.

And because of that, because cyber defense is going to need to grow, the US is going to need to provide competitive AI for cyber defense. It is a classic arms race scenario.

And so the US cannot simply step back and pause and turn off AI. It is already everywhere in the world. Therefore, the risks are rising. Therefore, we need to increase our investment in AI to maintain our cyber defense capabilities, both at the enterprise level and at the government level, and potentially even at the civilian consumer level.

So I think that the cyber defense necessity actually mandates that we continue to build out data centers to support it.”

END OF AN ERA. A NEW CHAPTER AWAITS.

As you’ve probably heard, I’ve said goodbye to CryptoPunk #8348 for $5.9M.

This wasn’t an easy decision. I spent months flip-flopping on whether to sell, but after more than six years, I felt it was time. This Punk became my identity, so there was a lot more to think about than just the price.

I wanted to write this earlier, but the transaction literally happened in a beer tent at Oktoberfest... So I needed some time to collect my thoughts.

The 2021 NFT mania was insane. It gave me the opportunity to explore digital identity in ways I never expected when I bought 8348 in 2020 for $18,000. I DJ’d across Europe, North America and the Middle East, worked with luxury brands including Louis Vuitton, Swarovski (with mmERCH) and Dolce & Gabbana, and helped curate art events in Miami, Ibiza and London. I also released original music, vinyl records, merchandise, and much more.

Looking back, I accomplished a lot with this Punk. 

But the landscape has changed considerably since then, and my interests and priorities have evolved too. Over the last 12–18 months, I’ve been winding down parts of the Seedphrase business and refocusing on what’s next. That’s meant going back to my roots in trading, which was my focus before 2020, taking on new challenges in gaming with Wolf Game, and exploring new possibilities with AI. 

On the creative side, I want to see what I can do under my own name. DJing without a helmet, playing more of my own taste in music, and being more involved in the art scene as Danny. I’ve spent six years building an identity around 8348, and I’m ready to give myself a bit more freedom to explore outside of that.

I’m proud of what we built with this Punk. Selling it doesn’t change that, or my interest in the space. There’s still plenty I want to do here.

I won’t reveal the new owner’s identity. They’re welcome to come forward in their own time. One of the first things I asked was that they be a good custodian of such a legendary CryptoPunk, and they’ve assured me they will.

8348 has been a huge part of my life since 2020. It’s strange to move on from something so many people know me by, but I’m excited to put that same energy into what comes next. 

You’ll be seeing more of me. Just without the helmet (and with fewer traits).
